q: Do you use pure black for text or backgrounds?
new_q: Do text and backgrounds avoid pure black (#000000)?
pass: Fewer than 4 visible text elements and at most 1 background use pure black #000000. Dark greys (#111 to #333) and brand dark colours count as soft.
fail: 10 or more text elements, or 3 or more backgrounds, use pure black.
niche: Luxury and streetwear brands sometimes use pure black on purpose as brand identity: still flag it, but as low priority.

q: Do button and link labels start with a verb and convey urgency (e.g., "Shop Now")?
new_q: Does the main add-to-cart button start with an action verb?
pass: The main button starts with an action verb in its ready state: Add to cart, Add to bag, Buy now, Shop now, Order, Get yours, Book. Urgency words are a bonus.
fail: The main button has no verb ("Cart", "Basket", "In winkelmand", "Checkout") or is a vague label ("Submit", "Continue", "OK").
niche: "Select a size" / "Choose an option" is a temporary state before a variant is picked: judge the label after picking.

q: Does the footer display social media links?
pass: The footer links to at least one social profile (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, Pinterest, LinkedIn, X).
fail: No social profile links in the footer.

q: Is the most common size/color preselected?
new_q: Is a default variant preselected, so the shopper can add to cart right away (except sizes in fashion)?
pass: Fashion: the colour or style is preselected (label "Colour: X", highlighted swatch, or one product page per colour) and the size is left to the shopper. Other products: a default or best-selling option (scent, flavour, pack size, model) is preselected and the button works right away.
fail: Fashion: a size is preselected (wrong-size orders and returns). Other products: nothing is preselected and the button is disabled until the shopper picks every option.
na: The product has no variants, or the only variant is size in fashion.
niche: Fashion: never preselect size. Food, beauty, supplements: preselect the bestseller or the subscription option the brand wants to push.

q: Is lazy loading enabled for images and videos?
pass: At least 30% of images load lazily (loading=lazy, data-src or a lazy class), and the first visible images do not.
fail: Fewer than 30% of images are lazy, so the page downloads images shoppers may never see.
na: Fewer than 5 images on the page.

q: Are product titles and descriptions concise, informative, and consistent?
pass: The title names the product clearly (brand or line, product type, key variant) in about 60 characters or less, and the description explains what it is and why it matters in short paragraphs or bullets.
fail: The title is cryptic or stuffed with keywords, or the description is missing, one vague line, or a long wall of text.
niche: Fashion titles can be short brand names ("The Essential Jacket") as long as the type is clear.

q: Are product ratings displayed near the product title?
pass: Stars or a score AND a review count are visible right above or below the title (first screen, near the price).
fail: No rating near the title, or a rating without a count, or reviews only further down the page.
na: Brand-new product with zero reviews is still a fail (show the store rating instead). Not relevant only for made-to-order B2B quotes.
niche: Fashion and home: a store-level rating (Trustpilot, Google) near the title also passes.

q: Is there a short list of key benefits highlighted near the product title?
pass: 2 to 5 short benefit points (icons, ticks or bullets) sit between the title and the add-to-cart button.
fail: Benefits only appear in the long description below the fold, or there are none.
niche: Fashion: fit, fabric feel and care benefits count ("breathable", "machine washable").

q: Is the product’s material or composition information clearly provided?
pass: Materials, fabric, ingredients or composition are stated on the page, including inside a tab or accordion.
fail: Nothing on what the product is made of.
niche: Beauty and food: ingredients list. Fashion: fabric %. Furniture: materials and finish. Electronics: specs replace composition.

q: Are before-and-after images included to demonstrate the product’s effectiveness?
pass: At least one before/after image or comparison is shown in the gallery or on the page.
fail: The product promises a visible result but shows no before/after.
na: Products without a visible effect: fashion, furniture, food, electronics, accessories.
niche: Only applies to beauty, skincare, hair, health, cleaning, fitness and similar.

q: Are video testimonials available on the product page?
pass: At least one video of a real customer or creator talking about the product (UGC, TikTok-style, review video).
fail: No customer videos (brand-made product videos do not count).
niche: Low priority for luxury and furniture; high for beauty, supplements, gadgets.

q: Is the free shipping threshold (if applicable) highlighted near the main CTA?
pass: The threshold amount ("Free shipping over €50") is shown near the price or button, or free shipping applies to every order and that is stated there.
fail: A threshold exists (announcement bar, cart, policy) but is not shown near the button, or shipping is not mentioned at all near the button.
na: Free shipping is not offered at all and never will be (then the shipping cost should be shown instead).

q: Are trust signals like secure checkout badges positioned near the CTA?
pass: Within the buy box: payment logos, secure checkout, guarantee, returns or warranty mentions.
fail: No reassurance near the button (only in the footer or checkout).
niche: Returns and guarantee lines count as trust signals, not only payment logos.

q: Are product prices and any discounts clearly displayed?
pass: The price is visible in the first screen next to the title; a discount shows the old price struck through or the saving.
fail: The price is hidden, tiny, below the fold, or a discount is not made visible.
na: Price on request (B2B, made to order).

q: Is the product gallery easy to navigate with arrows or swipe functionality on mobile devices?
pass: On mobile, the gallery shows it can be swiped (dots, progress bar, peek of the next image, arrows) or stacks the images.
fail: On mobile, one image with no sign that more exist, or tiny arrows only.

q: Is the breadcrumb navigation clearly visible?
pass: A breadcrumb (Home / Category / Product) or a clear back-to-category link is visible above the product.
fail: No breadcrumb or back link.
niche: Mobile: a short "< Category" back link is enough.

q: Is there a visible newsletter subscription form in the footer?
pass: An email field to join the newsletter sits in the footer or just above it.
fail: No email signup at the bottom of the page.

q: Does the footer include links to customer support options (e.g., live chat, help center)?
pass: The footer links to at least one of: contact, FAQ / help center, shipping, returns, live chat.
fail: None of these in the footer.

q: Does the footer have a "Back to Top" button for easy navigation?
new_q: Is there a back to top control on long pages?
pass: A back to top button or floating arrow appears on long pages.
fail: No back to top control on a page longer than about 4 screens.
niche: Low priority overall: keep it, but it should never be a top finding.

q: Does the cart icon display the number of items currently in the cart?
pass: After adding one item, the cart icon shows "1" (badge, number or "Cart (1)").
fail: After adding one item, the icon shows no number.
na: The add-to-cart test cannot run (non-Shopify, bot wall): then "couldn't check", never fail.

q: Is there a quick access link to the cart?
pass: A cart or bag icon/link is in the header on desktop and mobile.
fail: No cart link in the header.

q: Does the footer include store location or contact information?
pass: The footer shows an actual phone number, email address or street address.
fail: Only a "Contact" link, a store-locator link or town names.
niche: Brands with physical shops: the address or a store locator with addresses passes.

q: Is there a clear and accessible "Search" button or icon?
pass: A search icon or field is visible in the header (on mobile it may sit behind the menu only if the store has fewer than about 20 products).
fail: No search, or search hidden deep in the mobile menu on a large catalogue.

q: Are all important pages linked in the main navigation?
new_q: Does the main navigation focus on the pages that make money?
pass: The main menu links to the money pages: main categories or collections, new, bestsellers, sale. Contact, About, Returns and FAQ live in the footer.
fail: Main shopping categories are missing, or the menu is overloaded (more than about 10 top-level items) or led by non-shopping pages.

q: Do some images include annotations?
pass: At least one gallery image has callouts, labels or text pointing at features or benefits.
fail: No annotated image, while the product has features worth explaining.
na: Fashion (apparel, footwear, bags, jewellery) and art or decor where the look is the point.
niche: High value for electronics, gadgets, furniture with mechanisms, sports gear, beauty with ingredients.

q: Are dropdown menus easy to use on both desktop and mobile?
pass: Menus open on tap and hover, items are big enough to tap, at most 2 levels deep.
fail: Tiny tap targets, 3+ levels, menus that close while moving the mouse.
na: Product page scan: always "couldn't check" until the scanner opens menus.

q: Is the logo clickable and linked to the homepage?
pass: The header logo links to the homepage (or the language homepage).
fail: The logo is not a link or links elsewhere.

q: Have you tested "color swatches" vs. "small images" of variants for the best user experience, especially in fashion?
new_q: Do colour variants show as image thumbnails or clear swatches?
pass: Colour or pattern variants show as small product images or accurate colour swatches, with the name on hover or below.
fail: Colours only as a text dropdown or tiny unlabeled dots.
na: Products with one colour or no visual variants.
niche: Whether they tested it cannot be seen from the page: the rewrite judges what is shown. Fashion and home decor: image thumbnails preferred for patterns.

q: If the product includes additional items as a pack, are all included products visually displayed?
pass: For packs, sets and bundles: every included item is listed or pictured near the button ("What's included").
fail: A pack or set without a clear list of what is inside.

q: Is the main product title visually prominent?
pass: The title is the largest or one of the largest texts in the buy box, in the first screen.
fail: The title is small, below the fold, or competes with other headings.

q: Does the product page have clickable tabs for easy access to more product details?
pass: Details are organised in tabs or accordions (description, size and fit, shipping, ingredients...).
fail: All information is one long text block, or details are missing.
na: Very simple products with a short description (fewer than about 80 words).

q: Are some images displayed with products key selling points and/or badges (e.g. vegan, cruelty-free, etc.)?
pass: At least one gallery image carries badges or selling points (vegan, award, bestseller, key claim).
fail: Gallery images are photos only, while the product has strong claims to show.
niche: Strong for beauty, food, supplements, eco products, gadgets.

q: Does the product page display thumbnails for quick navigation through the image gallery?
pass: Desktop: a strip or grid of small clickable preview images beside or under the main image, or all images shown as a scrollable grid.
fail: Desktop: a single image with only dots or arrows, so shoppers cannot see what other images exist.
niche: Mobile is judged by the swipe checkpoint instead.

q: Does the product gallery include videos to demonstrate the product?
pass: A product video (in use, demo, unboxing, fit on body) is in the gallery or right below it.
fail: No product video.
na: Never (but low priority for simple consumables).
niche: High value for gadgets, furniture, fitness, cooking products; fashion: a short on-body clip.

q: Are product images shown from multiple angles and perspectives to give a complete view?
pass: At least 3 images showing different sides or views (front, side, back, top, detail, on body / in room for scale).
fail: 1 or 2 images, or several near-identical shots.

q: Do product images include lifestyle shots that show the product in use?
pass: At least one image shows the product being used, worn or in a real setting.
fail: Only packshots on a plain background.
niche: Fashion: on-model shots count as lifestyle.

q: Is there a section explaining how to use the product in simple steps?
pass: A "How to use" section, steps, or a usage video.
fail: The product needs instructions and none are given.
na: Clothing, shoes, bags, jewellery, furniture, decor, simple food (eat it).
niche: Applies to beauty, skincare, supplements, coffee and food prep, tools, electronics, cleaning.

q: Are relevant cross-sell or up-sell products displayed on the product page?
pass: A related, complete-the-look, routine or upgrade section shows other products on the page.
fail: No other products suggested anywhere on the page.

q: Do all product images have consistent backgrounds to maintain a professional appearance?
pass: The product-only shots share one background style. Lifestyle and model shots are expected and do not count against it.
fail: Product-only shots mix different backgrounds (white, grey, coloured, cut-out) without a system.

q: Are there images showing the product alongside complementary items?
pass: At least one image shows the product with other products the shopper might also buy (styled outfit, product with accessories, part of a routine).
fail: The product is always shown alone.
na: The parts of the product itself, its packaging or its case do not count; products that are never used with others.
niche: Fashion: an outfit styled with other sellable pieces passes. Beauty: routine shots pass.

q: Do you offer quantity discounts?
pass: The price per item drops when buying more (2 for X, 3+ save 15%, bundle tiers, subscribe and save).
fail: Quantity options with the same price per item, or no multi-buy offer. A sale price or "save X%" is not a quantity discount.
na: Products people buy once (furniture, large appliances, one-off fashion items).
niche: High value for consumables: beauty, food, supplements, pet, cleaning. Fashion basics (socks, tees) qualify; most fashion does not.

q: Do you offer a quick complementary add-on upsell near the main CTA?
pass: A one-click add-on next to the button (checkbox or small card: case, refill, care kit, warranty, gift wrap).
fail: No add-on near the button (a recommendations carousel further down does not count).
